name: Jorja Smith
notes: The lane's UK-soul flagship, moving between neo-soul, lovers rock and UK-garage tempos. The entry gives three drum variants and says "the switch between these is her defining arrangement habit" — a single model states one placement, so **variant (1) is what is encoded**: "a soft programmed soul kit, kick on 1 and 3½, clap on 2&4, sparse hats", which is `secondaryAnchor` 3&, a layered clap-snare and a non-continuous 16th hat at a fill density of 0.28. The one-drop and the 130–140 two-step are recorded here and deliberately not authored: the one-drop needs a beat-3 placement the Lane line does not carry, and the garage shuffle needs its own swing. The band is therefore the entry's stated "72–108 straight, backbeat on 2&4 for the soul material" and stops there: the separate "130–140 two-step/garage" subset is a different kit and a shuffled backbeat, so carrying it in the band would have emitted 109–129 — a range the entry gives to nothing — and would have paired 130–140 with the straight soul kit the research assigns to neither. She is one of the seven models in this section with an 808 — "sub-808 with long decay on the R&B material, played electric bass with lovers-rock root-and-fifth motion on the reggae-facing cuts, and a filtered sine-sub on the garage tracks" — so `drums.bass808` is authored with role **counter_riff** and a low slide probability, keeping the played bass alive alongside it. Harmony is "m9 colour and 2-to-4-bar cycles; jazz-derived voicings on the ballads and modal one-chord vamps on the up-tempos", so no families and a vamp-weighted harmonic rhythm. Melody is "smooth mid-alto with a distinctive straight-tone, slightly flat-leaning delivery, low-to-moderate note-density, and short repeated hook phrases; backgrounds are close and narrow" — the riff-loop structure and the least dense counter of the modern models here. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are every drum and 808 number, `bpm.mode` 92 (the entry gives no per-track readings, so the centre is a reading of the band, not a quote), and all melody figures; the research marks the tempo bands and drum patterns as idiom inference and [LOW-CONF].
